claim: The reference P/D disaggregation deployment uses 4 replicas of TP=1 vLLM for prefill and 1 replica of TP=5 vLLM for decode, both belonging to the same InferencePool and distinguished via the llm-d.ai/role label.
quoted_support: The prefill Deployment is 4 replicas of TP=1 vLLM - labeled with llm-d.ai/role=prefill. The decode Deployment is 1 replica of TP=5 vLLM - labeled with llm-d.ai/role=decode.

claim: NIXL supports TCP transfer but high-bandwidth networking (InfiniBand, RoCE, or EFA) is highly recommended for production P/D disaggregation usage.
stance_target: RDMA-class networking is a practical requirement for production P/D, not just Kubernetes-pod networking
quoted_support: NIXL supports TCP transfer, but high-bandwidth networking (IB, RoCE, EFA) is highly recommended for production usage.

claim: Long-context workloads at a 10:1 input-sequence-length to output-sequence-length ratio, on medium-to-large models, are the workload profile where separating prefill and decode into separate instances is justified.
quoted_support: For long context workloads (10:1 ISL:OSL) and medium-to-large models, separating prefill and decode into separate instances enables: Improved throughput via specialization...

claim: P/D disaggregation observability treats prefill and decode as independently scaled pools joined by NIXL KV transfer, so pool balance and transfer health are the primary signals to monitor rather than a single aggregate latency metric.
stance_target: operational monitoring model for disaggregated deployments
quoted_support: P/D disaggregation runs prefill and decode as independently scaled pools joined by a NIXL KV transfer, so the signals that matter are pool balance and transfer health rather than a single aggregate latency.
